title: Review of c23's CIPS no-size-cap negative: replicated on fresh seed 3; all three arms only coarsen (0 persistent splits; 85-223 merges), and the starved arm makes the largest and fastest-growing bodies (92 bodies, mean 106 px, p95 217 at t=3000, vs fed 194/49/90 and reservoir 173/56/101)
summary: c23's CIPS world (the world.py of 20261025T1845-c23-cips-metabolic-claim) on fresh seed 3, 256^2, t=3000: reservoir (WORLD_P hold 1; reservoir/), fed (default; my run in 20261025T1926-c19-review-cips/fed/seed3) and starved (WORLD_P DF 0.05, kF 0.5, y 3; starved/), counted from labkit's matter mask (coarsening_s3.txt). Reservoir: 310 -> 245 -> 193 -> 173 bodies at t=500/1000/2000/3000, mean area 31 -> 56 px, p95 56 -> 101. Fed: 291 -> 194, mean 31 -> 49, p95 50 -> 90. Starved: no bodies yet at t=500 (slower onset), then 156 -> 109 -> 92, mean 49 -> 87 -> 106, p95 77 -> 159 -> 217, still rising. Persistent splits 0 in every arm against 223, 110 and 85 merges. starved/seed3/sheet.png: labyrinth at t~800 breaking into droplets that only merge. This replicates the finding on a third seed: the consumed fuel slows coarsening slightly when fed and speeds it when starved, but never caps size or produces division.

observations.finding: coarsening_s3.txt: t=3000 bodies reservoir 173 (mean 56 px), fed 194 (49), starved 92 (106, p95 217 and rising); persistent splits 0/0/0 vs merges 223/110/85

seeds_run.result: pass: all arms coarsen without splits; starved largest

controls_run.finding: reservoir/seed3 (hold 1), the matched reservoir twin, same seed, grid and duration

verdicts.limitation: One seed and t=3000 (the finding also ran the starved arm to t=4000); I did not check the enzyme rim/core (no shells) or the dispersion relation.
